posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body:
1. If you have a question, try googling it first (also, read the manual and do the turorials).
2. If you ask for help, don’t write a rambling question, but clearly state the question/problem AND post screen shots (not cropped) of what you have done.
3. “Can this thing be done in RPG Maker?” Yes, but if it’s something complex not having to do with 2d jrpgs, it’ll take coding (and probably look janky).
4. “I want to make Zelda/Fire Emblem.” Google ABS or SRPG plugins.
5. “Which RPG Maker should I get?” Don’t get anything older than MV. MZ has layer mapping, a lot of added QoL features (more than most MV people realize) and runs better, but it’s lacking some plugin options and many of its plugins are obfuscated and more expensive.
6. “Can you help me with this AI code?” No.
7. “What’s the script for…?” There’s a thread in here with a link to the script call list.
8. “Can I change this or that in this obfuscated (for example VisuStella plugin) that’s not in the settings?” Probably not.
9. Read plugin instructions and add your plugins in the correct order in the plugin list.
10. You can add functions etc to the game as plugins by saving a notepad file with a .js extension.
11. Some of your plugins may be using some switches and variables (usually in the 1-10 range by default). Don’t use those for other things.
12. You can use google translate to google for foreign plugins too (like Japanese ones, that usually have English instructions).
13. If you make changes to your game and nothing’s happening, test it by starting a new game instead of loading saves. Also, use the game playtest to test battles instead of the battle test.
14. There are playtest options like allowing you to move through any tiles when holding Ctrl, or changing switches and variables with the F-keys.
15. The highest numbered event page that has its conditions fulfilled is the one that is active.
16. If you use ‘erase event’, the event will be back when you leave and re-enter the map.
17. Use one control event to control your cutscenes (all the move routes, switches etc).
18. There’s a thread in these forums called “A Guide to Damage Formulas”. Read it if you have questions about them.
19. A troop event won’t run after the last enemy is killed.
20. Parallel common events don’t run in battle.
21. “How to make my battlers do cool moves?” Yanfly/VisuStella action sequences.
22. Yanfly/VisuStella/ATT_Turan plugins let you put notetags in states that run at a certain time in battle.
23. “Is there a tileset for this?” Google.
24. You can place tiles without the auto-effects by holding shift when you place them.
25. You can copy/paste when mapping with the right mouse key (hold it, select area, place with left key).
26. Your sprites can be any size. The sheets are formatted into 8 - 4x3, or 1 - 4x3 if the filename starts with the $-sign.
27. ”How do I make conditional choices?” Google conditional choices plugin.
28. ”How do I make fast travel?” Give the player hidden items with location names and have your event ask for select item from the hidden item list.
29. "Can I make event on event trigger?" Not without plugins.
30. "How to make my NPC disappear in a cutscene?" Give the NPC a page 2 with empty graphic with a condition for a switch. Then you turn the switch ON in your cutscene event.
31. "I need to check with event touch when through is ON!" Use a parallel event to put the coordinates of the event and player into variables and make conditionals comparing those.
32. It's good to use wait times in parallel events that check something, unless the check needs to be done constantly.
33. "How to make a QTE in battle?" With action sequences or a QTE plugin.
34. "I can't move my character!" Check if you have autorun events (or a common event set to autorun) running. You need to use erase event on your autorun event or switch them to another page, or else they continue to repeat from the beginning (for the common event turn off the switch). [also, check your tile passabilities]
35. If you have an unknown plugin conflict, you should trace it by methodically turning plugins (or groups of plugins) off and checking when it’s resolved, to find the culprit.
36. Don’t make changes to the core js files. If you update your project, they will be rewritten. It’s also much easier to see and remember what changes you’ve made, if you’ve made them through the plugin system.
37. “How do I move my followers in cutscenes?” You can get a plugin or you can turn the followers off and show and move them as events in the cutscenes.
38. “I want a different item effect depending on the target (one of my party members is a ROBOT!)” You can set up a more complicated damage formula, or you can have the item add an empty state and then run a common event that checks for the state on an actor and applies the effects. Or get a plugin.
39. “I want to restrict who can be selected as target for skills or items.” For MV there’s Yanfly selection control. Unfortunately, there’s not a VisuStella version of it. Search other plugins (Caethyril maybe had one).
40. Learn the base engine and events first. Don’t mindlessly fill your project with plugins you don’t need, but don’t be afraid of them either.
41. “What’s a...?”
Yanfly:
Singlehandedly made most MV plugins. No longer active.
VisuStella:
A group who ported most of Yanfly stuff to MZ + made more plugins.
Plugin:
Extra code added to your game in a coordinated way.
Notetag:
<...> in your notes which plugins may use to read stuff.
QTE:
Quick Time Event.
42. Remember to add credits. Read terms of service for any materials you use (may differ between commercial and non-commercial use). You can’t use copyrighted material even in a hobby game without permission. Getting donations from a free game is commercial use, unless the terms of service state otherwise.
43. You can’t crack anyone’s encrypted game and no one here will help you do it. You also can’t translate someone’s game without their permission.
44. What is RTP? It just means the default graphics/sound packed with the RPG Makers. It’s origin “run time package” is from a time when download size was an issue and people would download the assets just once, independent of the games (the games didn’t include them).
45. When you reference a game in a support question, don’t assume people know the game. Explain the mechanic and post screenshots or videos.
46. “I added assets but they aren’t working!” Google RPG Maker asset standards.
47. Parallax mapping in RPG Maker world means using a picture as a map. You can bind a parallax pic to the map by starting the filename with a ‘!’, but since you usually want to control multiple layers, get a plugin like Galv’s Layers.
48. Special characters in front of your file names: ‘!’ in character sheet doesn’t shift the sprite up and affects star tile interactions, ‘!’ in parallax binds it to the map, ‘$’ in character sheet makes it a single actor sheet
49. “How do I change a tile to reveal a secret passage?” You can show the tile as an event and then use a switch to change it to an empty page.
50. Your boat can move in sea tiles, your ship can move both in sea and deep sea tiles (positions shown in standard overworld tileset). If you set them as passable, the vehicles cannot move there.
51. Some positions in the tilesets are reserved for special use (like the autotiles and the sea tiles). Read the built in guide for that!
52. “How do I restrict where my NPCs can walk?” Get a plugin, like Yanfly region restrictions or VS Events & Movement Core.
53. If you make your damage formulas run code (like change switches or variables), the game will run that when evaluating auto battle moves.
54. It’s good practise not to put stuff after the transfer player command (to another map) in an event (even though some commands might still run after it).
55. You can’t move an event to another map. What you can do is turn a switch to turn the event to an empty page on map 1 and turn an event to a page with a graphic on map 2.
56. Only the current map is loaded. You can’t control events on another map (but you can affect switches/variables that may control what happens when you transfer to a new map).
57. “How do I make the title screen do stuff?” Get a plugin that controls the title screen or allows you to make an evented title screen.
58. “How do I make my enemies more intelligent?” Yanfly/VisuStella Battle AI plugin.
59. There are files in the img/system folder where you can change the icons, windowskin, state layouts, balloons, affect colors etc.
60. There are base materials that aren’t included in the files with new game. If you bought your game from STEAM, you can find them in the game folder DLC folder. The materials include full body pics of the characters.
61. State rate means the rate you’ll be affected by them, not inflicting them. There’s the ‘attack state’ trait if you want your normal attacks to inflict states when attacking with a certain weapon for example.
62. If your skill is ‘Certain Hit’ and adds a state, it will ignore the state rate of the enemy.
63. (De)Buffs and States are different things. Buffs and debuffs increase/decrease a parameter by 25%, can stack two times and counter each other.
64. The damage value is the last number in the damage formula (if you want to do other stuff in the formula, do it before giving the damage value).
65. If you’ve made custom options with Yanfly/VisuStella that you want to reference, you get it with ConfigManager.yourSymbol
66. Important assets tip 1! whtdragon (weapons + animals + base sprite emotes and animations).
67. Important assets tip 2! Avery (variety of materials + edits + tutorials for mapping in particular).
68.
LINK
to a thread how to use VS Battlecore target to accept a variable.
69. Some plugins may have problems handling files if you encrypt them.
70. Data is stored in objects, where you can get values or run method functions with a dot ‘.’ In some cases you can use simpler references to the objects, like a/b in damage formulas or user/target in some plugins. For custom battle stuff you can add your own properties in the objects during battles.
71. Random encounters are based on average steps. Bush tiles increase the rate x2, driving a ship decreases the rate to 0.5.
72. Special tiles/settings:
Region Id:
Number 1-255 you can place on a tile on the map.
Terrain tag:
Number 1-7 you can assign to a tile in the tileset.
Star tiles:
passable but drawn on top of character.
Bush tiles:
character bottom translucent.
Ladder tiles:
character faces up.
Counter tiles:
Talk to dudes behind tables.
Damage tiles:
...they damage you.
73. “I want cool battlers/enemies!” Akashics, ShadowHawkDragon, Low, Thalzon, Holder (and others).
74. “I want on map enemies!” You can set events with event touch battle processing and give them move routes + control their move routes to move toward player/stop chase. Set them on an empty page when you kill them (you can also control their respawn). Or just get a plugin.
75.
LINK
to a thread with hit/damage flowchart
76. Weather effects and BGS persist on map change. To stop them you can set them to none on the new map with an autorun event (or BGS w/map properties).
77. Player touch events trigger only when you move on to them (not transfer of jump).
78. You can select a specific frame on the sheet in move routes with events (direction is 2/4/6/8, X is 0 left, 1 middle, 2 right):
this.setDirection(direction); this._originalPattern = X; this.resetPattern();
LINK
to a thread w/plugin to also do it with gameplayer.
79. Scripts to change battle BG mid battle (you can also get a plugin). [these for for MZ at least]
Code:
SceneManager._scene._spriteset._back1Sprite.bitmap = ImageManager.loadBattleback1("NAME");
SceneManager._scene._spriteset._back2Sprite.bitmap = ImageManager.loadBattleback2("NAME");
80. If you want to wait for player input in a cutscene, an easy way to do it is to show an empty and transparent text box in the bottom.
81. If page conditions change, all other pages will run their events to the end, but parallel pages will change instantly.
82. States outside of battle will run their regeneration effects (like poison) every 20 steps.
83. Important assets tip 3! Galv’s plugins. Galv’s Layers is really useful, the best option for parallax mapping. Galv’s Projectiles allows cool map skills and minigames and they have a lot of other plugins as well.
84. You can put moving map elements on the map, by placing them as events and putting stepping on, using Yanfly/VS doodads (or DragonBones stuff).
85. Event autonomous move routes stop if the player is outside range. You can set the moves in other ways or use plugins to change that.
86. Here’s an example of a way to run VisuStella commands in script form, for JS notetags (shown in another linked thread already, but anyway):
let name = "VisuMZ_1_BattleCore";
let command = "ActSeq_Element_AddElements";
let addEle = JSON.stringify([`2`]);
PluginManager.callCommand(this, name, command, {
"Elements:arraynum" : addEle
});

posts.author: alice_gristle
posts.body:
rpgLord69 said:
19. A troop event won’t run after the last enemy is killed.
Click to expand...
Din't know this!
So if I have a troop event that, say, restores my immortal vampire boyfriend's all HP at every turn end, it doesn't do so after the last foe has been offed?

posts.author: Robro33
posts.body:
alice_gristle said:
Din't know this!
So if I have a troop event that, say, restores my immortal vampire boyfriend's all HP at every turn end, it doesn't do so after the last foe has been offed?
Click to expand...
nope. the game checks to see if the fight is over and ends it before it looks to see if any event pages are triggered. even if your event's trigger was the enemy's hp being 0%, if theyre the last one then the event wont go off because the player already won.
the usual suggestions are to use a plugin to allow it, or to make any enemy with a 0% hp trigger have an immortal state placed them at the start of the fight and use the event to remove the state, run the rest of the event, and then kill the enemy.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Very nice list. I would humbly suggest another one.
If you don't have experience, don't immediately download a bunch a plugins just because that is what "everyone" suggests or "everyone else" is using. Learn what the engine can do through Events and even scripting first. Then selectively download and test one plugin at a time that seems to do what you can't do with Events and Scripting or that the plugin can just do easier.
Personally, I think that would help a lot of new users, but that could just be my jaded opinion.

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
First off, thanks for your efforts. I also thought about some kind of collection of "quick tips", like tips and tricks explained in one sentence each. But I didn't know where to start.
Your approach is a little different, but I'll share the thoughts I had with these kinds of lists.
The longer the list gets, the less likely a beginner will read through it. They are keen to start, they are motivated, they want to jump right in.
Some points are oddly specific, and a beginner won't probably understand what a "Yanfly", "QTE" or an "ATT_Turan" even is.
Also, some entries in the list seem to be less forgiving and reflect more of an expert's perspective, dealing with this question on a daily basis for years already.
If I imagine a use case of someone asking a question, and will be forwarded like "Didn't you read the New User Manual?". So they check it out, and find their question on like position 50, and it says "google it".
Maybe, it can be some more like a "I wish someone had told me when I started" collection of short "Did you know" facts, that are fun to read and everyone will learn at least something. Also maybe categorized by experience, as some entries are more advanced than others.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Here is another one that a new person using MZ probably wouldn't know.
For some reason, when you make a new project, the Pictures Folder in the IMG Folder of the project only contains upper body busts of the characters. If you want to have access to the full body images that are available, you have to go to the Main MZ Folder, DLC Folder, BasicResources Folder, and Pictures Folder and add them manually to the appropriate folder in your project.
I can't remember how long it took me to find out that those full body images where available, but it was quite a while.
